There exist distinct actual partition-forest laws with K=1 when the spectral set meets the core and 1<=K<=|T| otherwise. Their root block equals v log2(s)+v delta+r(E K-v) +E sum_roots log2(1/rho_l), with 0<=r(E K-v)<=p I(g)/2 and v delta<=(log2 e) 2rp E B. Thus normalized common-core rarity overhead is at most (log2 e) I(F), leaving base rarity and all remaining coding costs unpaid. For disjoint private conjunctions rho_l=2^-w_l and Q=product(1-rho_l), E K-v=4p^2 Q(sum rho_l-(1-Q)). All E are unconditioned spectral-weighted sums over nonempty sets; entropy units are bits. A fixed complete-reference scale prior lambda^(j)=2^-j lambda, w_j=1/((j+1)(j+2)) pays v for selecting j=0.
